/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 42-year-old man is being treated by his female family medicine physician for chronic depression. Recently, he has been scheduling more frequent office visits. He does not report any symptoms or problems with his SSRI medication during these visits. Upon further questioning, the patient confesses that he is attracted to her and says "You are the only one in the world who understands me". The physician also manages his hypertension. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

Options:
A. Re-evaluate this patient for borderline personality disorder
B. Ask closed-ended questions and use a chaperone for future visits
C. Immediately tell this patient that you can not continue to treat him and avoid any further communication
D. Increase the dosage of this patient’s SSRI
E. Petition the medical ethics committee board that you wish to date this patient

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns managing a patient's romantic feelings toward a physician, which falls under psychiatric treatment and professional boundaries."}
